stimulus.text:
“I long to hear that you have declared an independency — and by the way in the new Code of Laws which I suppose it will be necessary for you to make I desire you would Remember the Ladies, and be more generous and favourable to them than your ancestors. Do not put such unlimited power into the hands of the Husbands. Remember all Men would be tyrants if they could. If perticuliar care and attention is not paid to the Laidies we are determined to foment a Rebelion, and will not hold ourselves bound by any Laws in which we have no voice, or Representation.”
— Abigail Adams to John Adams, Braintree, March 31, 1776 (abridged; spelling as in the original)
stimulus.source_note: Abigail Adams to John Adams, March 31, 1776. Public domain.

books.section: Topic 3.6 The Influence of Revolutionary Ideals, B. Evolving Ideas on Gender

stem: In this letter, Abigail Adams most directly asks her husband to

options.text: Grant women the right to vote in the new republic
options.misconception: She never asks for the vote here; she asks about married women's standing under the new laws.

options.text: Limit husbands' legal power over their wives in the new laws
Free the enslaved people held by Massachusetts families
options.misconception: The letter is about wives, not enslaved people; Adams writes about husbands' power, not slavery.

options.text: Refuse to sign any code of laws Congress writes
options.misconception: She wants the new laws written fairly, not refused; she asks John to shape them, not block them.

rationales.B: Adams asks for laws that do not put “unlimited power into the hands of the Husbands.” Her request is about wives' standing under the law, not the vote or slavery.
rationales.A: The vote never appears in the letter; Adams asks about the power of husbands, not the ballot.
rationales.C: Slavery is not her subject here; the letter argues about wives and husbands, not enslaved people.
rationales.D: She urges John to write the new laws well; refusing to sign them is the opposite of her request.
rationales.general:
1. Read what she asks for. New laws that are “more generous and favourable” to wives than the old ones.
2. Find the power she names. The “unlimited power” of husbands over wives.
3. Rule out the bigger asks. She never mentions voting or freeing enslaved people in this letter.
